Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Gray
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 01/27/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 95 as introduced could delay collection of certain court costs from former inmates by 180 days after release from custody. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Gray
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/02/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 95 as amended and reported by the Committee on Judiciary could delay collection of certain court costs from former inmates by 180 days after release from custody and requires former inmates to enter into a repayment plan with the jurisdiction or jurisdictions in which he or she has financial obligations within 30 days or releases. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Gray
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/18/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 95 as passed the House of Representatives could delay collection of certain court costs from former inmates by 90 days after release from custody and requires former inmates to enter into a repayment plan with the jurisdiction or jurisdictions in which he or she has financial obligations within 30 days of release. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Gray
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/23/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 95 as passed the House of Representatives could delay collection of certain court costs from former inmates by 90 days after release from custody and requires former inmates to enter into a repayment plan with the jurisdiction or jurisdictions in which he or she has financial obligations within 30 days of release. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Judiciary, provides for an 180-day period, after release from physical custody, that an inmate would have before certain court costs are required to be paid.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary
